title: Hunting Missy's Killer
description: An in-depth investigative feature examining the cold case murder of fitness instructor Terri "Missy" Bevers inside a Midlothian church.

blocks.text: A church murder stunned the community. Eight years on, the case is still unsolved — by Lisa Howells

On 18 April 2016, 45-year-old mother of three Terri "Missy" Bevers arrived at the Creekside Church of Christ in Midlothian, Texas. A popular and charismatic fitness instructor for Camp Gladiator, Missy had scheduled an early-morning workout class for 5:00 AM. Outside, a torrential rainstorm lashed the town. Unlocking the main doors at around 4:18 AM, she carried her fitness equipment inside the quiet building, completely unaware that she was not alone.

Just half an hour earlier, at approximately 3:50 AM, the church's internal surveillance cameras had captured an eerie figure wandering through the corridors. Dressed head-to-toe in tactical police-style SWAT gear — complete with a heavy helmet, vest with "POLICE" emblazoned on the front and back, gloves, and shin guards — the intruder was casually roaming the hallways, opening doors and prying open lockers using a claw hammer.

When Missy walked into the church foyer, she crossed paths with the intruder. At 5:00 AM, her students arrived for class only to find the church doors unlocked and Missy lying unresponsive in a pool of blood in an interior hallway. Emergency responders rushed to the scene, but Missy had suffered catastrophic puncture and blunt force trauma wounds to her head and upper torso. She was pronounced dead at the scene.
The Chilling Video and the Distinctive Walk

The murder sent shockwaves through Midlothian, a peaceful town south of Dallas. Investigators immediately released the church's CCTV footage to the public in hopes that someone would recognise the killer's distinctive gait. The footage revealed an individual walking with a pronounced, slight limp and feet splayed outward — a gait that forensic podiatrists suggested could indicate a previous injury, a physical impairment, or simply ill-fitting tactical gear.

Initial speculation debated the killer's height and gender. Law enforcement initially estimated the person to be between 5ft 7in and 5ft 9in, but later acknowledged the suspect could be shorter, ranging from 5ft 2in to 5ft 8in, and could be either male or female. The heavy tactical gear obscured all facial features, body shape, and hair, leaving police with only the footage and the murder weapon as direct clues.

Detectives examined whether this was a burglary gone tragically wrong or a targeted assassination. While nothing of significant monetary value was taken from the church, the intruder had spent nearly thirty minutes vandalising glass doors and display cases before Missy arrived. Some criminologists posited that the staging of a burglary could have been an intentional facade to mask a premeditated murder.

Surveillance cameras from a nearby sporting goods store recorded a suspicious vehicle circling the area in the hours prior to the murder. A silver or light-coloured 2010–2012 Nissan Altima was seen driving slowly around the parking lot at around 2:00 AM, flashing its lights and pulling into secluded parking bays before disappearing into the night.

Detectives executed dozens of search warrants spanning cellular tower dumps, social media accounts, and text messages. Forensic analysis revealed that Missy had received flirtatious and creepy messages on LinkedIn and other social platforms in the weeks leading up to her death. Search warrants also scrutinised personal and financial relationships, though family members and close acquaintances were rigorously interviewed and cleared.

Despite over 3,000 investigative leads, multiple DNA tests on forensic samples retrieved from the crime scene, and thousands of hours of review by the FBI and Texas Rangers, no suspect has ever been formally charged. The Midlothian Police Department maintains an active tip line and insists the case will never be closed until justice is served for Missy and her daughters.

Eight years later, the mystery of Creekside Church remains one of the most haunting unsolved murders in modern American history. For true crime sleuths and veteran detectives alike, the image of the cloaked intruder wandering the dimly lit church corridor with a hammer remains a chilling testament to a crime that defied easy answers.

Missy's family and the Midlothian community continue to honour her vibrant life and legacy as a devoted mother, mentor, and athlete, holding annual memorial runs and keeping her memory alive while awaiting the crucial tip that will finally identify the figure in the helmet.
